findings.title: Test cleanup references non-existent alias "alias" instead of the actual IDP alias
findings.body: The cleanup lambda `testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove` uses the literal string "alias" instead of the dynamically generated alias `"idp-alias-" + i`. This means the cleanup will attempt to look up and remove an IDP with alias "alias" which does not exist, so the 20+ IDPs created by this test will never be cleaned up. This can cause test pollution and interference with other tests that assume a clean realm state. The same bug exists on line 425 for the additionally created IDP.

findings.title: getLoginPredicate may throw NPE if IdentityProviderModel.getConfig() returns null
findings.body: The newly added predicate clause `idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC)` will throw a NullPointerException if `getConfig()` returns null. While most IdentityProviderModel implementations initialize the config map, the predicate is now used in the cache invalidation path (`registerIDPLoginInvalidation`) which is called during create/remove operations. If any code path constructs an IdentityProviderModel without initializing the config map, this would cause an unhandled NPE during cache invalidation, potentially leaving the cache in a stale state.

findings.title: getForLogin returns results in non-deterministic order due to HashSet
findings.body: The `getForLogin` method collects resolved identity providers into a `HashSet<IdentityProviderModel>` and returns its stream. HashSet provides no ordering guarantees, so the returned stream order is non-deterministic. While the current known caller (`OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean`) sorts results, any other caller of `getForLogin` that relies on a stable order (e.g., for pagination or display) would get inconsistent results across invocations. The same pattern exists in `getByOrganization`, but since `getForLogin` is a new public API surface, it's worth considering using a `LinkedHashSet` to preserve the delegate's ordering.
